newsitem.title: SYRIA: Lebanon admitted to regional power grid.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon admitted to regional power grid.

text.p: Electricity ministers of Syria, Jordan, Iraq, Egypt and Turkey, ending a meeting in Damascus on Thursday, have agreed to add Lebanon to an electricity network that will link up the five states by the year 2002, sources at the meeting said.

They said the ministers welcomed a request by Lebanon to join the network, part of an ambitious $2 billion plan to be partially financed by the Kuwait-based Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development.

The five states had approved a plan to establish the joint grid three years ago. Since then they have been holding regular meetings to discuss progress in each individual country and review joint efforts to complete the project. Lebanon's minister of electricity and water resources, Elias Hobeika, attended the meeting in Damascus.

Under the plan Jordan and Egypt will complete linking their electricity grids by December 1997, Jordan and Syria by July 1998, Syria and Turkey by July 1997, Syria and Iraq by the year 2000 and Iraq and Turkey by 2002.
The sources said the joint grid of the five plus the new member Lebanon would later be linked with the north Maghreb countries through Egypt and with Gulf Cooperation Council States via Jordan.
